newsitem.title: UK: SIB review of LME - summary of recommendations.
newsitem.headline: SIB review of LME - summary of recommendations.

text.p: Following is the text of a summary of recommendations made by the UK Securities and Investments Board (SIB) in its review of the London Metal Exchange (LME).
HISTORIC PRICE CARRIES (HPCs)
- The LME should review its rules relating to HPCs (and other Non-Market Price Transactions) to ensure that they are in line with best practice in other markets.
- The LME should review its systems to ensure that it is able to identify all trades effected away from the market price.
THE MEMBER/CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIP

- The LME should review, and amend where necessary, its rules and procedures to ensure that it can determine the exact relationship between its members and their customers in respect of each transaction and that appropriate regulatory obligations apply.
- The LME should review with the SFA what information it might collect to assist the SFA and itself in monitoring compliance with all appropriate regulatory obligations.
- The LME should consider the implementation of video and audio surveillance to bring the LME into line with best practice on other UK derivatives RIEs (Recognised Investment Exchanges).
NON-REGULATED CUSTOMERS

- The LME should pursue its plan to review and amend its rulebook so as to seek to afford the LME greater access to information about and, where possible, jurisdiction over its members' business, such as large positions they may hold, whether on-exchange or OTC.
WAREHOUSING ARRANGEMENTS
- The LME should undertake a thorough examination of those aspects of its warehousing arrangements which caused concern from respondents and which are of relevance from a regulatory perspective.
PAPERLESS TRANSFER OF WARRANTS
- The LME should undertake a study of the costs and benefits relating to the introduction of an electronic, paperless system for the transfer of warrants.
PRE-TRADE PRICE TRANSPARENCY FOR FUTURES TRADES
- The LME should take steps to ensure that the Vendor Feed system is kept up to date.
- An independent body should review the system of rebates of net incomes to those members who contribute to the Vendor Feed system.
POST-TRADE TRANSPARENCY ON THE LME
- The LME should publish indicators of price and volume in relation to inter-office trading which are drawn from its existing systems.
TRANSPARENCY OF OPTIONS TRADING
- The LME should take steps to improve both pre-trade price transparency and post-trade price transparency of options trading.
TRANSPARENCY OF WAREHOUSE STOCKS
- The LME, as part of its examination of certain aspects of warehousing, should consider what further information it could publish for the benefit of market users and with what frequency.
IDENTIFICATION OF PRICE MANIPULATION
- The LME should review its approach to the use of its extensive powers to regulate its market, in light of any guidance on what may constitute market abuse issued by the SIB's Market Conduct Group.
REPORTING OF LARGE POSITIONS TO REGULATORS

- The LME should carry out a detailed review of its information systems, particularly those for the receipt and processing of regulatory information, to ensure that it can quickly identify large on-exchange positions.
- The LME should seek to collect and review information on warrant ownership.

- The LME should carry out further work to consider the relative costs and benefits of publishing information such as concentration ratios which may alert the users of the Exchange to large positions.
INFORMATION SHARING

- The LME should ensure it is able and willing to cooperate with other regulators in exchanging relevant regulatory information, subject to the applicable legal constraints and taking fully into account the regulatory needs of others.

- The LME should implement formal, written procedures to ensure that there is consistency in its approach to the exchange of information with other bodies and in particular, that where appropriate a written record of information shared or received is maintained.

- The LME should discuss with the SFA how their existing Memorandum of Understanding may be augmented to ensure that the regulatory responsibilities of both parties are fulfilled and that the LME considers the implementation of written procedures in support of this aim.
- The LME should formalise arrangements with the LCH (London Clearing House) which aim to ensure that in appropriate circumstances large positions on the LME are promptly communicated to the LCH.
INVESTIGATIONS AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES
- The LME should introduce formal written procedures covering the investigation of potential rule breaches during inter-office trading.
COMPLAINTS
- The LME needs to distinguish clearly between disputes between members and customers, complaints against members and complaints against the exchange itself.
MEMBER INSPECTION VISITS
- The LME should establish and enforce a policy of pursuing disciplinary action where rule breaches are identified.
THE ROLE AND COMPOSITION OF THE LME BOARD
- The LME should review the composition and practices of its board to ensure that potential conflicts of interest between the LME's regulatory duties and its commercial interests are avoided.
THE ROLE OF THE BOARD

- The LME should review the board's relationships with its committees and with the chief executive and his staff with a view to much greater delegation to both of matters concerning the running of the exchange and market supervision and surveillance.
AVOIDING OR MANAGING CONFLICTS OF INTEREST
- a clear separation within the organisation between regulatory tasks and the commercial activities of the exchange, so that confidentiality of regulatory information can be seen to be preserved.
- The LME board should formally delegate responsibility for monitoring market trading and for intervening where necessary to maintain a proper market, so avoiding potential conflicts or interest.
THE ROLE AND COMPOSITION OF COMMITTEES
- The LME should review the composition of its committees.
- The full board should approve all committee appointments.

- The board should continue to set the terms of reference for each of the board committees, defining their delegated powers and scope, so that their routine decisions and actions do not generally need to be discussed in detail again by the main board.
- The LME should establish a Market Conduct Committee to oversee both the setting and routine enforcement of trading and contract rules and regulations on behalf of the Board.
THE ROLE, STRUCTURE AND RESOURCES OF THE LME EXECUTIVE
- A clearer relationship should be established between the board and the executive, primarily based on greater delegation of responsibility to the executive.
- A coherent strategy and supporting operational framework should be developed for the regulatory function on which the development of systems and the recruitment of staff can be based.
- Staffing in the Market Operations and Exchange Compliance departments should be increased.

- The regulatory and enforcement function should be given a sharper focus and higher profile at a senior level, through the creation of the post of Head of Market Regulation and Enforcement with the necessary experience, market expertise and reputation to command the confidence of the board and the members.
- The structure below the chief executive should be organised and strengthened to provide greater depth of management and clear functional separation.
- The LME should review its personnel policies to ensure it is in a position to attract and retain the necessary calibre of staff.
